note: Designated horse park in the badlands above the Little Missouri River, 20 mi north of Killdeer, with 81 corrals, a round pen and over 40 miles of horse and hiking trails. Camping is on open grass on the plateau; most sites have corrals. --Claude
summary: Park page + reserveNDparks: 31 sites on grass, 28 modern 30/50-amp electric only ($25/$30 Sat) and 3 primitive ($15). But 26 of the 31 are horse campsites (23 modern horse, 3 primitive horse); the only non-equestrian sites are 5 modern sites (14-18) inside the Main horse campground. No distinct non-equestrian campground: horse-camp question for the reviewer. Pay showers, vault toilets, dump. Closes November 1 (limited-service page).
flags: HORSE PARK (reviewer decides; possible drop candidate under the indistinct-horse-camp rule): the park page calls it 'one of North Dakota's designated horse parks ... set up with 81 corrals'. reserveNDparks types 26 of 31 campsites as horse sites: Canyon View (10 'Modern Horse Campsite', centroid 47.5479,-102.7360), Cove (3 'Primitive Horse Campsite', 47.5494,-102.7350) and 13 of Main's 18. The only non-equestrian units are Main sites 14-18 ('Modern Campsite'; 14-17 carry the remark 'No Corrals'), at 47.5461,-102.7355, in the same loop as the horse sites, not a separate campground. A 23-ft motorhome fits them (45-ft grass back-ins, 100-ft pull-through 18). The page does say 'Campers can enjoy both modern and primitive campsites' and lists all 28 modern sites without restricting them to riders; nothing on the page or in the reservation data says non-riders may not book a horse site. The stored note's 'regular modern campground of 28 electric drive-in sites' was wrong and is replaced.
